designSummary: Single-group before-and-after quantitative strand with all starters, and a qualitative strand analysed thematically; integration by joint display.
sampleSize: About 110 starters are expected by March 2027 and about 90 with a three-month score. With a standard deviation of change of about 16 points, 90 participants give a 95 percent confidence interval of about 3.3 points either side of the mean change, enough to tell whether the mean improvement is near the 8-point threshold in h1. For the interviews, 16 to 20 participants are planned, stopping when new interviews add no new barrier themes within each sampling group.
primaryAnalysis: Mean change in KOOS-12 summary score from baseline to three months with a 95 percent confidence interval among all starters, using multiple imputation for missing three-month scores and a complete-case analysis alongside.
secondaryAnalysis: Chair stand change; completion by age group, internet access and language with 95 percent intervals; reflexive thematic analysis of interviews by two analysts; a joint display comparing completion and outcome by subgroup with interview themes.
missingData: Three-month scores are sought by telephone from non-completers; the remaining missing scores are imputed using baseline score, age and attendance, with 20 imputations, and the number imputed is reported.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; subgroup completion rates are descriptive.
software: R for quantitative analysis; NVivo for coding.
overfittingGuards: Primary outcome and imputation model fixed before analysis
Subgroups limited to age, internet access and language
summary: About 90 three-month scores give a 95 percent interval of about 3.3 points; 16 to 20 interviews.
